abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.p: Over the past few decades, the trifluoromethyl group (CF3) has become one of the most prevalent in applied chemistry, frequently appearing in approved drugs and even more commonly in agrochemicals. However, this widespread use has led to the accumulation of trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) in the environment as a byproduct of metabolic and environmental degradation, prompting legislative actions to restrict certain chemicals and even entire compound classes of so-called “forever chemicals”. Hence, this has created a growing demand for alternative motifs that retain the beneficial molecular properties of the trifluoromethyl group but avoid forming trifluoroacetate during degradation. This review summarizes the current state of the application of trifluoromethyl-free, partially fluorinated fluoroalkyl groups in the development of drugs and agrochemicals. We focus on nine moieties that have shown presence in already approved and investigational structures. We also present data on fifteen innovative fragments promising for current and future research. We believe this guide will be valuable for industrial and academic researchers seeking sustainable and ecologically responsible solutions for biomolecular engineering, especially in applications that create risks of environmental pollution.
A compendium of alternative/replacement fluoroalkyl moieties to address the PFAS/“forever chemicals” problem stemming from CF3-containing industrial drugs and agrochemicals.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Over the past few decades, fluoroorganic chemistry has emerged as an essential component of modern drug discovery and agrochemical innovation, with fluorine incorporation enhancing chemical and metabolic stability, efficacy, and selectivity in small bioactive molecules.1–4 In pharmaceuticals, approximately 20–25% of marketed drugs now contain fluorine, a figure that has risen steadily since the early 2000s,5 culminating in 58 fluorinated small-molecule approvals by the FDA from 2018 to 2022 alone, representing about 23% of all new drugs in that period.6 Similarly, in agrochemicals, fluorine's prevalence has surged to over 50% of current products, with 127 fluorinated compounds registered out of 238 total agrochemicals between 1998–2020 (53%).7 This success positioned fluoroorganics as essential for addressing global health and agricultural challenges, though it raised novel environmental concerns about the accumulation and persistence of artificial fluorinated substances in the environment (Fig. 1A).8,9

sec.p: The environmental impact of perfluorinated compounds (PFCs) has been widely recognized, leading to legislative restrictions on their use in the European Union by the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) and globally under the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants.10 In 2023, several European countries submitted a novel proposal advocating for a complete ban on the use of per- and polyfluorinated alkyl substances (PFAS, “forever chemicals”) containing perfluorinated fragments as small as CF3– and –CF2– (with no halogen or hydrogen atoms attached).11 This proposal is expected to result in major EU-wide legislative action in early 2027, following the completion of consultation rounds. While the forthcoming EU-wide PFAS regulation does not explicitly include drugs and agrochemicals, legislative restrictions have already been applied to certain agrochemicals. For example, the CF3-containing herbicides flurtamone and flufenacet were discontinued in the EU due to their proven release of trifluoroacetic acid into soil and water (Fig. 1B).12,13 In 2025, Denmark banned the use of 23 pesticides, six of which contained a CF3-aromatic fragments, for similar reasons (Fig. 1C).14

The current legislative landscape highlights that the exceptional stability of fluoroorganic substances, once a groundbreaking advantage, has led to unintended consequences. While the resistance of polyfluorinated groups to chemical and metabolic degradation initially drove innovation, it now poses a serious threat to a sustainable and safe human environment. By 2020, over 50% of fluorinated agrochemicals contained a CF3 group in one form or another,7 placing the entire agrochemical industry under the looming threat of imminent legislative collapse. The challenge does not readily affect medicinal chemistry, but it may be a matter of a more distant time when similar restrictions will reach drugs and veterinary chemicals, especially in the case of bulk environmental release. This compels chemists to seek viable alternatives to the CF3 group, solutions that retain the benefits of fluoroorganic chemistry while preventing the release of trifluoroacetate and other persistent perfluoroalkyl substances into the environment.15 The shift of focus from CF3 chemistry to other types of groups appears completely inevitable in the years to come, which is why we decided to summarize the successful applications of alternative moieties primarily in drug discovery and agrochemical fields. We believe that such a summary will guide the readership in applying partially fluorinated alkyl moieties and will lead fluoroorganic chemistry into a more sustainable and stable long-term future. We would like to stress that it is not our intention to advocate for a complete abandonment of CF3-containing groups, which still drive innovation and seem unavoidable in the area of fine chemicals such as clinical drugs. Instead, our work provides information for critical analysis and aims to promote the diversity of fluoroorganic groups in practical applications.

sec.title: Fundamental aspects
sec.p: Fluoroorganic chemistry has accumulated a long and rich history in the design of bioactive molecules and bringing them to market. It is no longer the rare and exotic youngling who ambitiously disrupted the field a few decades ago, but rather an established integral part of contemporary chemical endeavor. This is why we won't recapitulate the most basic aspects that were already articulated in excellent reviews published a while ago (Fig. 2A),7,16–20 including one recent dedicated discussion of metabolic stability of fluorinated molecules.21 Nonetheless, one particular concept deserves special attention.

caption.title: (A) General features of carbon-fluorine versus carbon–hydrogen bond. (B) Lipophilicity assessment for partly fluorinated alkyl groups as proposed by Müller. An increase of the volume from the CH-to-CF exchange increases the lipophilicity, while the polarity of the resulting dipole vector decreases it. (C) Few selected cases of polarity effects in partly fluorinated groups.

sec.p: In the previous decade, Müller and Carreira published several influential experimental papers building on the idea of partially fluorinated alkyl groups.22–26 The works dealt with the polarity and conformational impact generated by sequential substitution of hydrogen atoms by fluorine in alkyl groups, moving from non-fluorinated to per-fluorinated ones via a set of intermediate partially fluorinated structures. In 2014, Müller proposed a simple and exceptionally instructive model for accessing polarity of aliphatic fluoroalkyls by considering two counteractive factors: an increase of molecular volume from each consecutive fluorination (increases lipophilicity), and a vector sum of the C–F dipoles creating a resulting polar dipole (decreases lipophilicity).27 The model helped predict lipophilicity, which is a key parameter introduced by stopper/terminal groups to complex organic molecules (Fig. 2B).

This approach has been expanded by subsequent excellent works from Linclau,28–32 O'Hagan,33–35 Grygorenko (Fig. 2C)36–40 and other groups41,42 including our modest contribution.43,44 While the contribution of fluoroalkyl groups to molecular volume reflects in their ability to bind to their target proteins and pockets, the lipophilicity remains a key parameter for assessing the potential impact of fluoroalkyl groups on permeability, metabolic susceptibility, and solubility of the eventual biomolecules.45,46 Thus, volume and lipophilicity are the two main parameters to look for when exchanging an alkyl substituent with various fluoroalkyl ones.

Other important fundamental contributions of fluorine to biomolecular design include its involvement in creating novel47,48 or modulating existing hydrogen bond sites,49,50 changes in pKa of the functional groups,40,51–56 as well as forming tetrel bonding57,58 and multipolar interactions within protein interiors.59 The conformational effects of fluorine on alkyl chains, such as its proclivity for adopting gauche-type vicinal conformations,18,19 have also been well characterized. However, these effects are more relevant to linker alkyl chains such as the one in GABA60 or alicyclic moieties such as fluoroproline in the structure of danicopan,61 while standalone terminal fluoroalkyl groups may be less sensitive to the inner gauche-effects owing to their free rotation.

In summary, the CF3-group is typically considered a compact and lipophilic addition to a given structure. With this in mind, we would like to move on to considering partially fluorinated groups in designing drugs and agrochemicals.

sec.title: CF3-containing fluoroalkyl groups
sec.p: A SciFinder search reveals that between 2001 and 2025, hundreds of thousands of papers and patents mentioned CF3-containing compounds (Fig. 3A). This trend continues to grow, with approximately 22k patents published in the past year alone. However, in many instances, the CF3-group acts as a part of more complex partially fluorinated fluoroalkyl moieties such as those depicted in Fig. 3B. Closer examination reveals that those moieties have become quite important players in modern biomolecular engineering. What made those moieties so successful? We will consider three examples.

(B) CF3-containing partially fluorinated alkyl groups that are trending in recent research. (C–F) Application of the CF3-containing groups in recently approved drugs. Here and below, the name of the protein from the PDB entry is indicated under the structure box.

sec.p: The first example that we would like to present in this context is lenacapavir, an HIV-1 capsid inhibitor developed by Gilead and approved by the FDA in 2025 for providing pre-exposure HIV protection that lasts for 6 months (Fig. 3C).62 It is clear that to provide such a prolonged period of activity, a critical parameter would be the metabolic stability of the drug in the body. The SAR study of lenacapavir has been published, revealing that introduction of the fluoroalkyl moiety at the last stages of optimization provided a significant contribution to the substance's in vivo metabolic stability, prolonging it severalfold compared to the methyl-containing analogue (Fig. 3D).63

The second example is vorasidenib (AG-881),64,65 an allosteric inhibitor of mutant isocitrate dehydrogenase developed for the treatment of glioma in 2024 (Fig. 3E). In this case, the trifluoroisopropyl moiety was chosen since it improved cellular potency, while also keeping low metabolic clearance.65,66 The symmetric structure of vorasidenib reflects the fact that it binds at an intermonomeric interface of the target protein homodimer. Structural studies have revealed that the two trifluoroisopropyl groups bind the same set of residues from the two separate monomers.65,67 At the same time, the CH3/CF3 faces of the fluoroalkyl group are bound slightly differently. While the trifluoromethyl group established contacts with polarizable side-chains of Trp124 and Met259 as well as the backbone carbonyl of Val255, the less polar methyl group was coordinated with a purely hydrophobic pocket, created by Val281 and Met259 (Fig. 3E).65,67 This underpins the ambivalent character of the CF3-group, which manifests in its competence in establishing close polar and polarizable contacts while maintaining overall lipophilic character. In fact, it is common that the trifluoromethyl group forms additional polar interactions, such as a C–F⋯H–S hydrogen bond with cysteine,68 a hydrogen bonding with histidine,69 coordination of fluorine with asparagine side-chain amide,70 coordination of the C–F bond with the amide backbone groups,70,71 and more.57,59

The third example is elexacaftor (VX-445), which was approved by the FDA (in combination with tezacaftor and ivacaftor) for the treatment of cystic fibrosis in 2019 (Fig. 3F). The substance acts as a type III corrector of the malignant mutation in the CFTR protein.72 A structural study has shown that elexacaftor binds to the transmembrane section of the target protein, while the lipophilic 3,3,3-trifluoro-2,2-dimethylpropoxy group protrudes into the lipid bilayer and binds to several hydrophobic residues at the interface of the transmembrane helix 11 and the lipid bilayer (Fig. 3F).73 This example illustrates the ability of the 1,1,1-trifluoro-tert-butyl to be lipid-like and serve as an interface molecule between the protein and lipid hydrophobic core.

As a lipophilic moiety, a CF3-bearing aliphatic group is often found to improve properties that involve crossing of biological membranes such as permeability, cellular potency,65,74–76 and/or CNS penetration.77,78 With many standard hydrocarbon groups, the tradeoff for such improvement would be hampered metabolic stability.45 However, CF3-containing groups are also well known for the concomitant metabolic stability improvements when replacing hydrocarbon moieties.66,69,76,78–80 In the frame of medicinal chemistry, the combination of these traits, improved permeability and metabolic stability, is considered highly desirable for a successful drug candidate.

In addition, some of the fluorinated groups have been conceptualized as bioisosteres of the tert-butyl groups with improved metabolic stability (Fig. 4A).80–84 For 1,1,1-trifluoro-tert-butyl74–76,80,85 and 1-trifluoromethyl-cyclopropyl82,86,87 the data have indeed shown that these moieties boost metabolic stability when replacing the tert-butyl moiety, while for 1-trifluoromethyl-cyclobutyl the opposite has been true in most reported cases (Fig. 4A).83,88,89 At the same time, the 1-trifluoromethyl-cyclobutyl group was introduced to the structure of atumelnant (CRN-04894), a nonpeptide melanocortin type 2 receptor that recently advanced to phase 3 clinical trials (Fig. 4B). In this case, the 1-trifluoromethylcyclobutyl fragment was chosen as a non-chiral aliphatic substitute for an ortho-trifluoromethylphenyl fragment as a method to reduce hepatic clearance while maintaining the original potency (Fig. 4B).90 In addition to bolstering the metabolic stability, fluorination of the tert-butyloxycarbonyl helps to evade its destruction by gastric acids (Fig. 4C),74 thereby promoting substances with oral availability, which is also highly desirable for modern drugs.

caption.title: (A–C) CF3-containing groups as stabilized analogues of the tert-butyl group and aromatics.

sec.p: On the downside of the CF3-containing groups remains their potential destruction towards trifluoroacetic acid. For certain fluoroalkyl groups, their metabolic degradation pathway has been well documented.91 For example, the 2,2,2-trifluoroethyl moiety, which is often found in approved drugs and agrochemicals, is usually metabolized by cytochrome P450 oxidases to form trifluoroacetaldehyde, which ultimately converts to trifluoroacetic acid.92–94 Thus, despite their growing presence in drugs, the CF3-containing groups may be less desirable for agrochemicals, which is why other groups are urgently needed to suggest alternative molecular substitutions.

sec.title: General considerations
sec.p: In our search for alternative molecular fragments, we identified a series of small, promising, partially fluorinated CF3-free alkyl groups (Fig. 5A, in green). These groups have a proven track record in the development of successful drugs and agrochemicals. For comparison, five CF3-containing moieties that were discussed in the previous section (Fig. 3B) are also included as reference points in Fig. 5A (in black).

caption.title: (A) The set of applied partially fluorinated groups selected for this review. The structures in each row are sorted by rising molecular volume compared to CF3. (B) A comparison set of classical groups. The molecular volume was calculated in molinspiration and compared to CF3; c log P lipophilicity index was calculated in MarvinSketch and compared to CF3; the number of papers and patents that report the moiety bound to a carbon atom by a substructure search in SciFinder (as of January 2026) for the time range 2001–2025 years.

sec.p: While the CF3 group dominates the patent literature (Fig. 3A), the statistical presence of the alternative CF3-free groups appears modest (Fig. 5A). Nevertheless, our search indicates that most of these alternative structures are referenced in thousands of patents, providing a substantial knowledge base for their application in biomolecular design. We assigned each alternative group by its molecular volume and calculated lipophilicity values (Fig. 5A), comparing them to a set of standard reference groups (Fig. 5B). While all selected structures are somewhat larger than the CF3 moiety, their impact on lipophilicity varies widely, ranging from −0.56 to +1.29 in c log P values. Notably, at least seven of these groups are smaller than the isopropyl moiety, which used to be considered a biological analogue of the CF3 group. In the following narrative, we will discuss each CF3-free alternative group in order of increasing molecular volume (Fig. 5A).

sec.title: 1-Fluoroethyl
sec.p: The 1-fluoroethyl group represents an established substituent, for which interest has been rising over the decades, especially in the patent literature (Fig. 6A). It can be found in drug candidates, agrochemicals, and in preclinical [18F]PET imaging agents.

caption.title: (A) General statistics regarding the 1-fluoroethyl moiety in papers and patents in the recent 50 years (SciFinder search as of February 2026). (B–D) Drugs containing the 1-fluoroethyl substituent that have advanced to clinical trials.

sec.p: In the 2010s, Novartis developed IDH-305, an allosteric inhibitor of mutant isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 connected to the development of cancer.95,96 They started with IDH889, which demonstrated good efficacy against the target but poor pharmacokinetic features (Fig. 6B). The optimization included two key changes, one of which was optimization of the alkyl substituent at the oxazolidinone ring. The (S)-1-fluoroethyl substituent showed the best efficacy while reducing metabolic clearance. Furthermore, it helped to lower lipophilicity, to reduce plasma protein binding, and to improve solubility. Notably, crystallographic analysis (Fig. 6C) revealed that the substance underwent a hydrophobic collapse, with the fluoroethyl moiety folding inwards to the rest of the molecule, forming van der Waals contacts with the central pyridine moiety. Drug candidate IDH-305 has undergone a series of clinical trials, including Phase 2 against glioma, but the development seems halted.

In the 2020s, Takeda Pharmaceutical developed rogocekib (CTX-712), an inhibitor of Cdc2-like kinases involved in the regulation of RNA splicing.97,98 They started with T-025, which previously demonstrated an excellent nanomolar activity but was characterized with an unfavorable ADMET profile (Fig. 6D).99 Several optimizations culminated in the variations of the alkyl substituent at the oxadiazole moiety. The 1,1-difluoroethyl moiety demonstrated the best balance between potency and metabolic stability, but suffered from low solubility. The solubility was restored with the (R)-1-fluoroethyl moiety. The eventual molecule rogocekib (CTX-712) progressed to Phase 1–2 clinical trials against acute myeloid leukemia in 2023.

The residue of the 2-fluoropropionic acid has been applied in the development of PET imaging agents.100 This residue is usually created from 2-bromopropionate esters, leading to a 2-18F nitrophenyl ester used for labeling of amines, most notably peptides (Scheme 1).101,102 Several structures such as [18F]Galacto-RGD103 and [18F]FPPRGD2 (ref. 104) have reached clinical trials; however, none of them has been approved for clinical use as of now.

caption.title: [18F]1-Fluoroethyl groups in PET agents that have advanced to clinical trials.

sec.p: 1-Fluoroethyl moieties can also be found in several prominent agrochemicals (Scheme 2). Flifenerim is a pyrimidine insecticide originally developed in the 1990s by Ube Industries (Scheme 2A).107 The substance acts presumably as an inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase, and has shown well-balanced temporal activity against several insect strains, which included fast onset and decay 2 days after treatment.108 Several pesticide structures have been derived from flufenerim, thereby the 1-fluoroethyl group showed the best performance in some cases,109 but it was replaced with difluoromethyl and ethyl groups in some others.110 In addition, flufenerim showed fungicidal activity, suggesting its use as a disinfectant against Candida auris biofilms, which may be useful for disinfecting in hospitals.111

caption.title: (A–C) 1-Fluoroethyl fragment in agrochemicals with reported paths of environmental degradation.

sec.p: Flucetosulfuron (LGC-42153) is a sulfonylurea herbicide developed by LG Life Sciences in the 2000s112 and marketed in several countries. This type of herbicide is known to inhibit acetolactate synthase, leading to a stall of amino acid synthesis. Studies of the flucetosulfuron degradation in water,113 soil114 and liver microsomes115 showed that the ester bond first undergoes cleavage, followed by breaking of the carbamate (Scheme 2B).

Indaziflam is a herbicide developed by Bayer CropScience in the 2000s,116 and approved for use in the US. The commercial samples have been reported to be based on 95+% concentration of a single diastereomer, which remains configurationally stable.117 The degradation of indaziflam has been studied, showing that the indane part of indaziflam is oxidized into indanone as well as the benzene-bound methyl to carboxylic acid, followed by formation of diaminotriazine (Scheme 2C).117 Other reports have claimed degradation markers that include the exchange of fluorine to a hydroxyl group or the elimination of hydrofluoric acid with the formation of an olefin.118–120

Lastly, it may be mentioned that 1-fluoroethyl group is isomeric to 2-fluoroethyl (–CH2CH2F). The latter is controversial moiety, which is notorious for the potential release of highly toxic monofluoroacetate under metabolic degradation.121,122 Despite that, [18F]2-fluoroethyl is found in several approved PET agents, e.g. [18F]Florbetaben and [18F]Flurpiridaz.123

sec.title: 1,1-Difluoroethyl
sec.p: The 1,1-difluoroethyl moiety is even more popular in biomolecular design, owing to the lack of chirality, making this substituent more predictable for screening and easier for production. This can be seen in generally favorable statistics of its occurrence in papers and patents, which surpasses 1-fluoroethyl while demonstrating continuous growth (Scheme 3A).124

caption.title: (A) General statistics regarding the 1,2-difluoroethyl moiety in papers and patents in the recent 50 years (SciFinder search as of February 2026). (B) Original semisynthetic preparation of vinflunine.105 (C) Semisynthetic preparation of omaveloxolone.106

sec.p: 1,1-Difluoroethyl has appeared in two semisynthetic drugs approved for clinical use in humans. Vinflunine is an anticancer substance from the Vinca alkaloid family developed in the Pierre Fabre Institute in the 1990s.125 The difluoroalkyl moiety was created by acidic derivatization of vinorelbine (Scheme 3B).105 The substance showed superior anticancer activity by acting as a specific inhibitor of tubulin,126,127 and was eventually approved by EMA for the treatment of advanced carcinoma in 2009. Omaveloxolone (RTA-408) is a semi-synthetic oleanane triterpenoid developed by Reata Pharmaceuticals (later Biogen) in the 2010s.128 It acts as an antioxidant inflammation modulator by activating the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 pathway.129 Omaveloxolone was approved by the FDA in 2023 for the treatment of Friedreich's ataxia, a rare neurodegenerative disorder. The substance was prepared from bardoxolone (RTA-401) by converting the acid group to the amine via a Curtius rearrangement, followed by acylation with 2,2-difluoropropiomic acid (Scheme 3C).106

Several other 1,1-difluoroethyl-containing drug structures have advanced to various stages of clinical trials (Fig. 7), including: nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs velsecorat (AZD-7594)130,131 and mizacorat (AZD-9567)132,133 developed by AstraZeneca (Phase 2), dihydroorotate dehydrogenase inhibitor DSM265 developed as an antimalarial drug (Phase 2),134,135 an estrogen receptor degrader LSZ102 developed by Novartis for the treatment of breast cancer (Phase 1/1b),136,137 a selective protein kinase C-θ inhibitor CC-90005 developed by Celgene/Bristol Myers Squibb for the treatment of autoimmune disorders (Phase 1),138,139 a formyl peptide receptor 2 agonist ACT-389949 developed by Actelion/Indorsia as an anti-inflammatory (Phase 1),140,141 complement factor 5a receptor 1 antagonist ACT-1014-6470 developed by Indorsia as an anti-inflammatory,142,143 and cannabinoid-1 receptor antagonist PF-514273 developed by Pfizer for the treatment of obesity (clinical trials claimed, phase unknown).144,145

sec.title: 2,2-Difluoroethyl
sec.p: Similarly to the previous moiety, its isomeric structure, 2,2-difluoroethyl, is highly represented in contemporary papers and patents (Fig. 8A). It can be found across investigational drugs and commercial agrochemicals. From the most recent cases, GS-CA1 is an experimental HIV-1 capsid inhibitor with high sub-nanomolar efficacy developed by Gilead (Fig. 8B).63,146 The substance represents an important milestone in the development of this type of drug, but was later taken over by an analogous structure GS-6207 (lenacapavir, see Fig. 3C),63 which eventually attained FDA approval for advanced pre-exposure HIV-1 prophylaxis in 2025.62 The structure is heavily fluorinated to block the metabolic hot spots and prolong the duration of the drug in the organism. Both GS-CA1 and lenacapavir bind to the HIV-1 capsid protein between the individual capsid subunits, thereby stabilizing the HIV-1 capsid assembly as a hexamer,147 and in this way preventing their translocation through the nuclear pores, thus preventing the early phase of the HIV-1 infection.148,149 It should be noted that in the SAR studies, structures containing the 2,2-difluoroethyl moiety showed excellent activity and metabolic stability profile, but they were eventually replaced by the 2,2,2-trifluoroethyl substituent that delivered even better target parameters (Fig. 3D and 8B).63 A co-crystal structure of GS-CA1 was reported bound to the capsid pentamer rather than the hexamer, and it shows the 2,2-difluoroethyl group positioned near the surface, in the vicinity of polar lysine residues from separate monomers (Fig. 8B). The hexamer capsid structure was crystallized with the final drug, lenacapavir, revealing that the corresponding 2,2,2-trifluoroethyl moiety was located near the surface, sandwiched between Lys70 and Thr107 residues.147 The surface location explains why the 2,2-difluoroethyl and 2,2,2-trifluoroethyl groups were interchangeable without the loss of activity.

(B) Experimental HIV-1 capsid binder GS-CA1 that was a milestone on the way to the development of lenacapavir. (C) 2,2-Difluoroethyl-containing compounds in clinical trials. (D) Experimental veterinary antiparasitic mivorilaner.

sec.p: A few compounds containing the 2,2-difluoroethyl group have advanced to clinical trials (Fig. 8C), including: highly selective 5-HT2C receptor superagonist bexicaserin (LP-352) developed by Arena (Phase 3),150 inhibitor of Rho-associated coiled-coil containing protein kinase 2 zelasudil (RXC-007) developed by Redx (Phase 2),151 and inhibitor of microsomal prostaglandin E synthase-1 vipoglanstat (GS-248) developed by Gesynta (Phase 2).152 In veterinary research, a blocker of GABA-gated chloride channels, mivorilaner (LY-3116151), has been investigated as an antiparasitic and antineoplastic agent (Fig. 8D).153,154 In addition, the 2,2-difluoroethyl group can be found in two commercial agrochemicals approved in both the EU and the US: penoxsulam and flupyradifurone (Fig. 9).

caption.title: (A and B) The two commercial agrochemicals containing 2,2-difluoroethyl moiety.

sec.p: Penoxsulam is a sulfonamide herbicide developed by Dow Agrosciences and commonly used in rice cultivation (Fig. 9A).155,156 Initial steps of microbial and photodegradation of this compound have been studied, revealing that it targets the triazolopyrimidine part of the molecule, converting it to the triazole as well as breaking the sulfonamide, while leaving the difluoroethoxy moiety stable.157–159 Penoxsulam acts as a noncompetitive inhibitor of acetohydroxyacid synthase by blocking the substrate access to the catalytic site. A crystallographic study has been conducted for penoxsulam bound to acetohydroxyacid synthase from a plant (A. thaliana) and a fungus (C. albicans).160 The 2,2-difluoroethoxy moiety was found close to the pair of Asp376–Arg377 residues, and one of the fluorine atoms was additionally coordinated to the hydroxyl group of Ser653 in the plant enzyme, while the fungal enzyme had the alanine residue at this position (Fig. 9A),160 suggesting that F⋯HO(Ser) contact might be the reason for the plant selectivity of the herbicide.

Flupyradifurone is a butanolide systemic insecticide developed by Bayer with low toxicity against honeybees (Fig. 9B).154,161,162 It is related to the neonicotinoid family of pesticides, acts as an agonist of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, and leads to paralysis of the insect nervous system.162 A structural study revealed that the 2,2-difluoroethyl moiety coordinates to Trp143, Val183, and Tyr192 of the target protein, while the CF2–H creates a peculiar donor–acceptor interaction with the tyrosine aromatic ring (Fig. 9B).163

sec.title: 1-Fluorocyclopropyl
sec.p: The literature on the 1-fluorocyclopropyl moiety exploded after 2018 (Fig. 10A), when the group of Ciulli introduced VH101 – a ligand for von Hippel–Lindau protein E3 ubiquitin ligase (Fig. 10B).164 The VH101 fragment has been widely used in the design of proteolysis targeting chimera (PROTAC) that utilize this ubiquitin ligase for selective degradation of malignant proteins.165 In the structure activity study, the introduction of the fluorine atom leads to a 2–3× increase in the binding affinity owing to the conformational preorganization of the cyclopropyl fragment.164 Notably, incorporation of the fluorine atom also improved permeability by a factor of 4×,164 which may be a result of a partial masking of the amide NH by the proximal fluorine atom (Fig. 10C). An example of a recent VH101-containing PROTAC is depicted in Fig. 10D.166

caption.title: (A) General statistics regarding the 1-fluorocyclopropyl moiety in papers and patents in the recent 50 years (SciFinder search as of February 2026). (B–F) 1-Fluorocyclopropyl moiety in medicinal chemistry research.

sec.p: From the other 1-cyclopropyl-containing molecules, SBI-553 deserves attention (Fig. 10E). This is an experimental drug designed as a CNS penetrant allosteric modulator of neurotensin receptor 1. The fluorination and the methylation of the cyclopropane moiety both improved the potency (Fig. 10E).167 The fluoro-substituted substance showed good oral bioavailability in mouse and rat, as well as CNS penetrability. These factors are critical for establishing therapeutic effects related to the treatment of CNS disorders such as schizophrenia or Parkinson's disease.167 A structural study showed that the fluorine atom established a contact with Arg167 (Fig. 10E).168

1-Fluorocyclopropyl fragment is found in the recently disclosed structure of cleminorexton (ORX-750), an orexin 2 receptor agonist currently developed by Eli Lilly and Centessa (Fig. 10F). The drug entered Phase 2-3 clinical trials for narcolepsy in May 2026.

sec.title: 2-Fluorocyclopropyl
sec.p: The interest in the 2-fluorocyclopropyl fragment has been steadily high since the 1990s (Fig. 11A) following the development of several ciprofloxacin-derived antibiotics by Daiichi Sankyo (Fig. 11B). One of these compounds, sitafloxacin (DU-6859),169,170 was approved for clinical use in Japan in 2008, whereas few others halted after preclinical and early clinical investigations, including: DK-507K,171 DX-619,172–174 DC-159a,174,175 DQ-113,176 and more.177

caption.title: (A) General statistics regarding the 2-fluorocyclopropyl moiety in papers and patents in the recent 50 years (SciFinder search as of February 2026). (B–F) 2-Fluorocyclopropyl moiety in medicinal chemistry research.

sec.p: In addition, two more structures recently reached clinical trials (Fig. 11C). The first example is cenacitinib (VTX-958), a selective inhibitor of tyrosine kinase 2 developed by Ventyx and used for the treatment of inflammatory disorders such as psoriasis and Crohn's disease (Phase 2).178 The proclivity of tyrosine kinase 2 inhibitors to incorporate the 2-fluorocyclopropyl moiety has been observed in other studies conducted by other groups, who showed that this moiety helped to improve the kinase selectivity and maintain high cellular potency.179,180 The beneficial effect of the 2-fluorocyclopropyl group was explained by a crystallographic analysis, which showed that a compact fluorine atom helped the moiety to pack beneath the residue Leu903, while at the same time, the local C–F dipole established the contact with proximal Arg901 (Fig. 11D).179 The second example is labuxtinib (THB-335, Fig. 11C), a selective inhibitor of c-kit tyrosine kinase developed by Third Harmonic & Novartis181,182 that recently underwent clinical trials in healthy participants (Phase 1).183

Several more interesting cases can be found in the recent literature, where a 2-cyclopropyl fragment helped to improve potency,184–186 to reduce hepatic clearance,186 and to improve solubility.185,187 For example, the group at Genentech optimized a reversible Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitor containing a terminal cyclopropylamide capping group. Introduction of fluorine helped to improve solubility and to lower lipophilicity, while maintaining the substance's activity and overall permeability. A crystal structure showed the location of the fluoroisoprolyl group near the entrance of the binding pocket, where the fluorine atom was oriented outwards and coordinated with several crystallographic water molecules (Fig. 11E).187 Here, the benefit of using a fluorinated moiety over the cyclopropyl and other aliphatic groups was clearly in the optimization of the general pharmacokinetic features of the substance rather than establishing specific interactions with the protein.

From the few cases of protein structures,179,185,187–189 one displayed a case where the 2-fluorocyclopropane moiety protruded deep inside the binding pocket.185 In the cocrystal structure of interleukin-1 receptor-associated kinase 4 bound to a highly potent inhibitor (IC50 0.1 nM), the fluorocyclopropyl was coordinated to Val200, Ala211, Lys213, and Tyr262 (Fig. 11F). This case underpins the versatility of the fluorocyclopropyl moiety in establishing interactions within a hydrophobic protein core.

sec.title: 2,2-Difluorocyclopropyl
sec.p: The 2,2-difluorocyclopropyl fragment has enjoyed rising popularity over the last decade (Fig. 12A). Compared to mono-fluorocyclopropyl groups, it is more lipophilic (Fig. 12B),28,32 and this is often used for making hydrophobic capping moieties, most commonly amides of difluorocyclopropanecarboxylic acid. Such structure can be seen in the two molecules that advanced to clinical trials. The first one, brepocitinib (PF-06700841), was developed by Pfizer190,191 as an anti-inflammatory agent and has entered Phase 3 trials for the treatment of dermatomyositis (Fig. 12C). It is a dual tyrosine kinase 2/Janus kinase 1 inhibitor that acts by blocking the signal of pro-inflammatory cytokines. In the SAR study, the difluorocyclopropyl caping group helped to establish a high level of selectivity toward the desired kinases. Crystal structures have been solved for the binding of the molecule to both target kinases, demonstrating coordination of the difluorocyclopropyl fragment by the same set of residues. These included Asp and Asn beneath the moiety facing its hydrogen atoms, Glu and Gly residues coordinating the fluorine atoms with their backbone groups, and a hydrophobic Val side chain (Fig. 12C).191 This coordination justified higher activity for the S-enantiomer, while the opposite R-enantiomer placed fluorine atoms pointing towards the polar Asp/Asn groups, which seemed unfavorable. Investigation of the substance's metabolism in human microsomes showed that all three primary metabolic schemes target the methyl-pyrazole part of the molecule, far away from the fluoroalkyl moiety.191

caption.title: (A) General statistics regarding the 2,2-difluorocyclopropyl moiety in papers and patents in the recent 50 years (SciFinder search as of February 2026). (B–E) 2,2-Difluorocyclopropyl moiety in medicinal chemistry research. (F) 2,2-Difluorocyclopropyl moiety in experimental agrochemicals.

sec.p: Another anti-inflammatory compound that has reached clinical trials is blovacitinib (TUL-01101), a Janus kinase 1 inhibitor developed by Zhuhai United Laboratories192,193 for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis (Fig. 12D). The group tested several capping moieties, selecting for the best selectivity to their target kinase against others from the Janus kinase group. Furthermore, the final compound showed low liver microsomal clearance, good permeability, and acceptable pharmacokinetics in mice, rat, and dog.193

Apart from these two prominent cases, not many optimized experimental pharmaceuticals contain the 2,2-difluoroisopropyl group.194,195 One interesting example is a brain penetrant inhibitor of leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 developed by Merck for the treatment of Parkinson's disease (Fig. 12E). Here, the replacement of the difluoroethyl moiety with 2,2-difluorocyclopropyl helped optimize several parameters, most notably augmenting metabolic stability, evidenced by an increased mean residence time in rodents, and improving cellular potency by an order of magnitude (Fig. 12E).195 Crystallographic data showed the location of the difluococyclopropyl group near the entrance to the binding pocket, with a fluorine atom coordinated with the backbone groups of Ser88 and Gly89 (Fig. 12E).195 This observation highlights the ability of the fluorinated moiety to participate in a multipolar type of interaction akin to a CF3-group.59

It is interesting that apart from the medicinal structures presented here, the 2,2-difluorocyclopropyl moiety can be found across the patent literature in a substantial number of experimental agrochemicals, examples of which are shown in Fig. 12F.196–200

sec.title: 2-Fluoroisopropyl
sec.p: The 2-fluoroisopropyl fragment has become increasingly popular in recent years (Fig. 13A) following the successful development of several interesting clinical candidates containing this fragment. This group is most commonly utilized as a metabolically stable analogue of terminal alkyl moieties: ethyl, isopropyl. However, in recent years several works included this group alongside CF3, showing rather promising results for bioactivity and metabolic stability.201,202

caption.title: (A) General statistics regarding the 2-fluoroisopropyl moiety in papers and patents in the recent 50 years (SciFinder search as of February 2026). (B–D) Examples of fluorination of the alkyl chain to suppress metabolic degradation.

sec.p: One of the most common uses of this moiety is blocking metabolic degradation pathways at the end of long alkyl chain fragments. The first such example can be traced back to the 1970s, when Merck developed 25-fluorocholesterol for blocking metabolic degradation of cholesterol (Fig. 13B). Cholesterol oxidases CYP125 and CYP142 perform oxidation of the terminal isopropyl moiety, which is why this group was fluorinated, producing a metabolically stable analogue maintaining general physicochemical properties of the original lipid.203 In the 1990s, Upjohn used similar reasoning for the development of trecetilide fumarate.204 They started with the structure of butilide, which is an established potassium channel blocker used as a class III antiarrhythmic drug (Fig. 13C).205 Fluorination at the end of the alkyl chain markedly reduced metabolic susceptibility in liver microsomes, while also altering the arrhythmic profile as measured in rabbit heart models.205 Compound advanced to clinical evaluation, but was later discontinued.206,207

In the 2000s, Merck discovered L-873724 as a selective cathepsin K inhibitor for the treatment of osteoporosis. The substance showed prohibitively high metabolic clearance in monkeys, while research in human hepatocytes identified leucine γ-CH as the major metabolic site prone to hydroxylation. Fluorination of this position produced odanacatib (MK-0822), which showed excellent selectivity against cathepsin K, while increasing the half-life in monkey from 2 to 18 hours (Fig. 13D).208,209 The substance advanced to numerous clinical trials (up to Phase 3), but was discontinued due to increased risk of stroke.210,211

In the 2010s, several companies developed selective estrogen receptor degraders based on a conceptually analogous molecular skeleton for the treatment of breast cancer. At least three structures included a 2-fluoroisopropyl moiety and have advanced to clinical trials (Fig. 14A): AZD-9496 (Phase 1),212,213 palazestrant (OP-1250) (Phase 3),214,215 and taragarestrant (D-0502) (Phase 3).216 It was shown that inclusion of the fluorine atom to the terminal isopropyl moiety helped to improve potency about 10-fold.213 Crystallographic analysis showed coordination of the 2-fluoroisopropyl group by Met388, Met421, Ile424, and Leu525 as the key hydrophobic residues (Fig. 14A).213,215,217 In addition to these structures, in the 2010s, Daiichi Sankyo developed a mutated isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 inhibitor safusidenib (DS-1001),218 that recently entered early Phase 1 clinical trials (Fig. 14B).

caption.title: (A–C) Further examples of the 2-fluoroisopropyl group in investigational drugs and agrochemicals.

sec.p: In the area of agrochemicals, triaziflam (IDH-1105) was developed by Idemitsu Kosan in the 1990s (Fig. 14C).219 This is a commercial herbicide that was used in Japan, but was later replaced by more efficient alternatives.

sec.title: 3,3-Difluorocyclobutyl
sec.p: The 3,3-difluorocyclobutyl moiety is yet another popular fragment trending in the recent literature (Fig. 15A). It is a component of an anticancer drug ivosidenib (AG-120), developed by Agios & Servier220 and approved in 2018 for the treatment of acute myeloid leukemia (Fig. 15B). It acts as an allosteric inhibitor of mutant isocitrate dehydrogenase 1, known for accumulating oncogenic metabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate.221 In the original SAR study, a cyclohexyl moiety was replaced with 3,3-difluorocyclopropyl to improve microsomal stability.221 Furthermore, a more recent structural study revealed that the inhibitor bound at the intermonomeric interface of the homodimer structure, with the fluorinated moiety protruding deep inside the allosteric site. It was located in the mostly hydrophobic pocket created by Leu120, Trp124, Val255, Met259, Ala258, Trp267, while the fluorine atom was coordinated with the backbone of Gln277 and the hydroxyl group of Ser280 (Fig. 15B).222 The coordination of the fluorine atom in the 3,3-difluorocyclobutyl group by polar residues has been reported in a few other crystallographic studies.223,224 A study of ivosidenib metabolism revealed that the drug remained unchanged in plasma, but an accumulation of degradation products was detected in feces and urine samples.

caption.title: (A) General statistics regarding the 3,3-difluorocyclobutyl moiety in papers and patents in the recent 50 years (SciFinder search as of February 2026). (B–F) 3,3-Difluorocyclobutyl moiety in drugs and experimental pharmaceuticals.

sec.p: From the thirteen identified metabolites, a few indicated modifications of the fluoroalkyl site (Fig. 15C).225 Lanisidenib (TQB3454) is an analogous isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 inhibitor developed by Chia Tai Tianqing, which advanced to Phase 3 trials for the treatment of carcinoma.226

Two other structures that contain the 3,3-difluorocyclobutyl moiety have reached Phase 1 clinical trials (Fig. 15E). These include vamagloxistat (ORF-229, BBP-711), an inhibitor of glycolate oxidase227 and IPN-60090, an inhibitor of glutaminase-1.228,229 In the latter case, the 3,3-difluorocyclobutoxy group was included for optimizing the overall profile, including cellular potency, microsomal stability, and solubility.229

Apart from these cases, the 3,3-difluorocyclobutyl moiety can be found across various medicinal chemistry optimization studies. Examples of optimized lead structures containing this moiety are shown in Fig. 15F.230–232 In addition, the 3,3-difluorocyclobutyl group can also be found across agrochemical patent literature alongside 2,2-difluorocyclopropyl mentioned earlier.197

sec.title: 1,1-Difluoro-tert-butyl
sec.p: The 1,1-difluoro-tert-butyl group has also shown a rise in the recent literature, although the overall numbers seem modest compared to other groups mentioned above (Fig. 16A). It is interesting to note that partial fluorination of the tert-butyl moiety has been used as a general approach to increase permeability (Fig. 16B)233 and metabolic stability234 in certain published cases. Furthermore, two structures containing this fragment have already reached clinical trials and showed promising results.

caption.title: (A) General statistics regarding the 1,1-difluoro-tert-butyl moiety in papers and patents in the recent 50 years (SciFinder search as of February 2026). (B–F) The use of the 1,1-difluoro-tert-butyl moiety in medicinal chemistry.

sec.p: Mefluleucine (NV-5138) was developed by Navitor for modulating the activity of a leucine sensor protein sestrin2, which activated the mTORC1 signaling pathway in the brain (Fig. 16C).235,236 The substance mimicked leucine and demonstrated high exposure due to high CNS penetrance, a lack of metabolic degradation (by branched-chain amino transaminase), and the absence of its utilization in protein biosynthesis.236 A crystal structure with human sestrin2 showed a coordination of the 1,1-difluoro-tert-butyl group in the hydrophobic pocket formed by Ile378, Leu389, Trp444, and Phe447 side chains. The CHF2 moiety demonstrated a peculiar C–H⋯imidazole coordination with His454 (Fig. 16C).236 The substance was a promising antidepressant, and it went to Phase 2 clinical trials.

Another drug structure containing this fragment, oditrasertib (DNL-788, SAR443820), was developed by Denali and Sanofi as an inhibitor of receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 1 for the treatment of neurodegenerative disorders (Fig. 16D).237 It is interesting that in Phase 1, the substance showed high brain penetrance similar to previous substances from this section.238,239 Nonetheless, the compound was discontinued later due to lack of efficacy. Recently, Merck developed an essentially similar inhibitor of this enzyme based on a bridged benzoazepine (Fig. 16E). The 1,1-difluoro-tert-butyl moiety was chosen as a means to suppress phase 1 metabolism that targets lipophilic moieties. The substance showed optimal pharmacokinetic and permeability features acceptable for CNS targeting. Crystal structure showed coordination of the 1,1-difluoro-tert-butyl by several hydrophobic residues, and a C–F coordination with the backbone carbonyl at Asp156 (Fig. 16E).240 Closer look reveals that one of the fluorine atoms participates in an intricate set of interactions (Fig. 16F), which involve an F⋯C

sec.title: Promising and rare motifs
sec.p: Previous sections make it evident that fluoroalkyl chemistry has advanced significantly, expanding the range of functional groups used in medical applications and, to a lesser extent, in agrochemicals. However, readers may have noticed that these groups represent only a small fraction of potential theoretical options. With this in mind, we would like to discuss several alternative fluoroalkyl motifs that hold promise for future research based on recent literature precedents and our intuitive analysis (Fig. 17).

caption.title: Rare and promising partially fluorinated fluoroalkyl motifs discussed in this section. The groups are ordered by increasing molecular volume. The molecular volume was calculated in molinspiration and compared to CF3; c log P lipophilicity index was calculated in MarvinSketch and compared to CF3; the number of papers and patents that report the moiety bound to a carbon atom by a substructure search in SciFinder (as of January 2026) for the time range 2001–2025 years.

sec.title: Ethyl-derived groups
sec.p: First notable motif that came to our mind is the 1,2-difluoroethyl moiety, which is structurally analogous to the more widely used 1,1- and 2,2-difluoroethyl groups (Fig. 18A). Importantly, the synclinal (gauche) F–C–C–F conformation maximizes the fragment's dipole moment, making this vicinal difluoro motif notably more polar compared to the geminal counterparts as seen from the experimental log P values (Fig. 18B).23,241 Recently, the Gilmour group claimed that the 1,2-difluoroethyl moiety acted as a hybrid bioisostere of the trifluoromethyl and ethyl groups. The team incorporated this fragment at the end of long alkyl chains in analogues of several drugs, such as fingolimod (Fig. 18C).242–244 To date, however, research on this motif has remained largely at the proof-of-concept stage, with only sporadic appearances in subsequent studies.245

caption.title: (A–C) Promising fluoroalkyl motifs: 1,2-difluoroethyl.

sec.p: Next, several innovative strategies could help replace the trifluoromethyl moiety. One promising approach is the reorganization of atoms (Fig. 19A).246 Previously, the Linclau group demonstrated that relocating fluorine atoms from the terminal CF3 group to penultimate positions significantly reduced lipophilicity (Fig. 19B).30 A group at AstraZeneca applied this principle to replace a CF3-group with a reorganized motif and smuggled an additional carbon atom into the estrogen receptor degrader camizestrant (AZD-9833). By replacing a 2,2,2-trifluoroethyl group (two carbons) with a 2,2,3-trifluoropropyl group (three carbons), they maintained comparable lipophilicity and potency (Fig. 19C).246

caption.title: (A–C) Promising fluoroalkyl motifs: 1,2,2- and 1,1,2-trifluoroalkyl by atom reorganization.

sec.title: Isopropyl-derived groups
sec.p: Among the previously discussed CF3-bearing moieties, 1,1,1-trifluoroisopropyl stood out as amongst the most promising (Section 3). However, the presence of a terminal CF3 group raises concerns about potential degradation into trifluoroacetic acid. This underscores the need for alternatives, such as the 1,1-difluoroisopropyl group (Fig. 20A).

caption.title: (A–H) Promising fluoroalkyl motifs: analogues of 1,1,1-trifluoroisopropyl.

sec.p: While this substituent has only appeared in a few experimental studies, it has already yielded promising structures (Fig. 20B).247,248 Several studies reported physicochemical data that allowed drawing an analogy between isopropyl, 1,1,1-trifluoroisopropyl, and 1,1-difluoroisopropyl groups (Fig. 20C and D).249,250

Regarding atomic reorganization (Fig. 20A), analogues representing this approach such as 1,1,2-, 1,1,3-, and 1,2,3-trifluoromethyl groups remain largely unexplored in the literature, with only a few patents reported for each (Fig. 20E).251–253 One interesting case that may be quoted in these regards is 4,5,5′-trifluoroleucine, which bears one of these reorganized groups at the amino acid side chain, and was reported recently (Fig. 20F).254

Another promising derivative of the isopropyl group is 1,3-difluoroisopropyl (Fig. 20G). It appears regularly throughout SAR studies and has delivered a few active experimental molecules (Fig. 20H).255,256 Curiously, compounds containing this moiety have shown good results in metabolic stability compared to alternative isopropyl-related groups when tested in liver microsomes256–258 and intravenously administered in rats.256,259 A docking study of a VEGFR-2 kinase active site with a 1,3-difluoroisopropyl-containing inhibitor revealed that the fluoroalkyl group was accommodated in a hydrophobic pocket, yet located close to Lys/Asp residues.255 It thus appears that the 1,3-difluoroisopropyl accumulates beneficial properties typical for fluoroorganic groups such as CF3, namely, it is a lipophilic moiety amenable to forming close polar contacts.

sec.title: Tert-Butyl-derived groups
sec.p: Another promising CF3-containing moiety is the 1,1,1-trifluoro-tert-butyl (Section 3), which has appeared in approved drugs before. Its analogous moiety, 1,1-difluoro-tert-butyl (Fig. 21A), although still not very common already appearing in only two drug candidates and was previously discussed in Section 4.10. Other important analogues of this group are the moieties with one, two, and three fluoromethyl groups, the latter (homo-CF3) representing the atom reorganization approach (Fig. 21A). Some of their use can be traced back to the early 1990s, when a group affiliated with Bristol Myers Squibb tested a few ciprofloxacin analogues bearing fluorinated tert-butyl groups.260,261 One of the things they noticed was a substantial reduction in the substance's lipophilicity from fluorination (Fig. 21B).261

caption.title: (A–F) Promising fluoroalkyl motifs: analogues of 1,1,1-trifluoro-tert-butyl.

sec.p: In 2023, the group of O'Hagan reintroduced the homo-CF3 motif by providing rather interesting information. For example, they showed that the lipophilicity of the tert-butyl group dropped with each consecutive fluorination (Fig. 21C). They also showed that the homo-CF3 group metabolized by oxidative defluorination, which is very useful in the context of the sustainable fluoroorganics (Fig. 21C). In addition, the homo-CF3 group showed interesting conformational organization governed by the electrostatic interactions between the C–F and C–H bonds within the moiety (Fig. 21D).35,262 Subsequent works from the O'Hagan and Grygorenko groups substantially enriched the arsenal of building blocks containing this moiety.39,262 Most recently, the group of O'Hagan introduced the homo-CF3 group to analogues of two drugs, elexacaftor and tezacaftor, and examined the associated lipophilicity effects.263

Other β-fluorinated tert-butyl analogues have also been applied in bioorganic engineering, where they demonstrated reduction of the substance's lipophilicity.233,256,261,264 For example, the group of Ohgane recently optimized degraders of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase. The team found that monofluorination of both tert-butyl moieties in their lead structure SRP3042 increased the activity while lowering lipophilicity to produce the optimized lead compound SRK2128 (Fig. 21E).264 Another interesting application of the β-fluorination is the reduction of the basicity of the adjacent amines. For example, a research group at Mitsubishi Tanabe optimized the structure of their melanocortin 1 receptor agonist by β-fluorination, which reduced the basicity of the pyrrolidine fragment, thereby increasing the Caco-2 permeability by two orders of magnitude (Fig. 21F).53 Unfortunately, this modification also reduced the intended activity and accelerated microsomal clearance, which is why it was abandoned in favor of other fluorinated amine structures.53 We may also add that the mono-fluoro-tert-butyl moiety may be considered for replacing 2-fluoroethyl group in order to block the unwanted metabolic degradation to toxic mono-fluoroacetate.

sec.title: Cyclic groups
sec.p: Lastly, we would like to mention a few of the promising cyclic fluoroalkyl residues. The first two structures that come to mind are 1-fluorocyclobutyl and 2,2-difluorocyclobutyl, which may be seen as analogues of 1-fluorocyclopropyl and 3,3-difluorocyclobutyl previously discussed in Sections 4.5 and 4.9, respectively (Fig. 22A).

caption.title: (A–D) Promising fluoroalkyl motifs: cyclobutyl-derived.

sec.p: Although still rare, the 1-fluorocyclobutyl moiety has appeared regularly in the medicinal chemistry literature since 2008.265,266 One interesting case is presented in Fig. 22B, when replacement of the 1-cyclopropyl group with cyclobutyl moieties yielded the best potency for 1-fluorocyclobutyl.167

The 2,2-difluorocyclobutyl motif was introduced by the group of Grygorenko in 2019.55 They prepared a set of 2,2-difluorocyclobutyl-containing molecular fragments. They also showed that the 2,2-difluoro modification reduced lipophilicity and improved aqueous solubility compared to the more symmetric 3,3-difluoro unit (Fig. 22C). The impact on pKa was also characterized (Fig. 22C). An experimental case published by Biogen illustrates improvements of general parameters with 3,3-difluoro to 2,2-difluorocyclobutyl substitution, especially with regard to aqueous solubility (Fig. 22D).250

The latest additions to fluorinated motifs are small bicyclic systems, among which bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane has been the most advanced in medicinal chemistry research, producing at least 6 drug candidates in clinical trials in recent years.267 This compact and rigid molecular fragment is especially effective in improving metabolic stability and solubility of biomolecules.267 Curiously, experimental works have suggested the application of the bicyclo[1.1.1]pentyl fragment as a bioisosteric analogue of the tert-butyl moiety.267–269 Thus, we can draw an analogy between mono- and difluorinated tert-butyl groups and mono-/di-fluorinated bicyclo[1.1.1]pentanes (Fig. 23A).

caption.title: (A–G) Promising fluoroalkyl motifs: bicyclo[1.1.1]pentyl-derived.

sec.p: Despite its most recent appearance in biomolecular research, the 3-fluorobicyclo[1.1.1]pentyl group has appeared in numerous patents and a handful of medicinal chemistry papers, where it revealed a particularly beneficial effect on metabolic stability of structures.270–273 For example, Lee et al. optimized inhibitors of dual leucine zipper kinase for treatment of chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, and found a potent substance with the bicyclo[1.1.1]pentyl-substituent. A study of the hepatocyte metabolism revealed that the bicyclopentane ring was a site for oxidative metabolism. Fluorination helped improve metabolic stability, while maintaining the same level of activity (Fig. 23B).271 A crystal structure revealed the location of the 3-fluorobicyclo[1.1.1]pentyl at the entrance site with the fluorine atom pointing towards the solvent (Fig. 23C).271 A group at Daiichi Sankyo previously developed DS21150768 as an orally active inhibitor of hematopoietic progenitor kinase 1 for cancer immunotherapy (Fig. 23D). The substance showed effective suppression of tumor in mouse cancer cell models.274

2,2-Difluorobicyclo[1.1.1]pentyl skeleton is one of the latest additions to the arsenal of fluoroalkyl moieties introduced independently by Merck275 and Enamine44 in 2019. It was originally introduced as a 1,3-substituted linker that mimicked the lipophilicity and volume of a para-substituted benzene fragment but improved its solubility (Fig. 23E).44,267 However, mono-substituted 2,2-difluorobicyclo[1.1.1]pentyl compounds have become available most recently (Fig. 23F), and these structures have already appeared in a couple of patents by Relay276 and Grünenthal.277 Curiously, this motif resembles the 3-difluoromethylbicyclo[1.1.1]pentyl group found in ZN-d5 (Fig. 23G).278 The latter compound is an inhibitor of the antiapoptotic Bcl-2 regulator protein and has been in Phase 1–2 clinical trials for amyloidosis and leukemia.279,280

Of course, the fluoroorganic groups presented here reflect our selection, and readers may notice the absence of some important motifs. In theory, the range of fluoroalkyl groups applicable to bioorganic engineering is vast, limited only by imagination and the creativity of synthetic chemists. We apologize for any omissions and acknowledge that not all possible motifs could be included. Nevertheless, we believe the selected examples effectively illustrate the most important concepts and therefore convey necessary background information for molecular engineering using small fluoroalkyl motifs.

sec.title: Conclusions
sec.p: Over the past decades, the range of fluoroalkyl groups used in drugs has expanded significantly, now including various partially fluorinated groups, both those containing CF3 and those without, as discussed in two dedicated sections (3 and 4) of our review. Novel agrochemicals featuring CF3-free groups have also emerged, such as substances containing 1-fluoroethyl (flifenerim, flucetosulfuron, indaziflam) and 2,2-difluoroethyl (penoxsulam, flupyradifurone) moieties, which have already reached the market. However, this remains an evolving field, and we anticipate that more structures will advance to commercial applications in the coming years.

To understand the requirements for fluoroalkyl moieties, it is essential to revisit the key properties that have contributed to the remarkable success of the CF3 group in the first place: this group is compact and lipophilic, highly resistant to metabolic clearance, and capable of engaging in both nonpolar and polar interactions within the protein interior of its targets. As highlighted in multiple examples throughout the review, many of these advantageous traits are preserved in other partially fluorinated groups. Additionally, these alternative fluoroalkyl motifs can offer further benefits, such as interactions involving polarizable adjacent C–H bonds. CF3-free groups may also enhance solubility due to their less symmetric topology compared to CF3. The primary potential limitation of fluoroalkyl groups is their steric bulk. However, our analysis identifies that many fluoroalkyl groups remain relatively compact. At least ten groups from Fig. 5A and 17 are less bulky than the isopropyl moiety, making them most viable candidates for CF3-replacement strategies, while the other moieties remain not much bulkier and can be considered for replacing bigger CF3-containing fragments.

However, it is important to note that the metabolism of innovative partially fluorinated groups has yet to be thoroughly investigated. While studies on the metabolic degradation of certain chemicals have been published, these often focus only on the initial steps, so-called metabolic hot spots. Given the PFAS regulations are currently developing and being implemented around the globe, it seems equally critical to identify the ultimate degradation products of fluoroalkyl groups, many of which remain stable beyond the initial few breakdown stages. Additionally, the current European PFAS definitions include –CF2– groups, a classification that may be justified in polymer chemistry, yet, the extent to which concerns about environmental persistence apply to smaller groups, such as 1,1-difluoroethyl (Section 4.3), 2,2-difluorocyclopropyl (Section 4.7), and 3,3-difluorocyclobutyl (Section 4.9), remains to be seen. We suspect that the definition might be too crude, and that more studies are needed to improve informed legislative decisions in the future. Even for the CF3-bearing groups, more detailed studies are needed to identify structures and conditions that may divert the degradation away from trifluoroacetic acid towards inorganic matter.
